package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious PDF document exploiting Foxit Reader)
package_info.package_versions: Foxit PDF Reader (affected versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The PDF document is crafted to exploit a design flaw in Foxit PDF Reader's warning dialogs, enabling the execution of arbitrary code by tricking users into accepting harmful default options. This leads to the download and execution of a remote payload, constituting a clear malware delivery mechanism.

execution_context.trigger: user interaction (after two warning dialogs in Foxit PDF Reader)
execution_context.file_location: malicious PDF file (embedded script or action)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PDF action/script that, after user clicks through two warning dialogs, downloads and executes a payload from a remote server.
malicious_snippets.code_language: PDF embedded scripting (JavaScript or PDF action)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user interaction (clicking through two warning dialogs), the embedded PDF script triggers a download of a remote payload and executes it on the victim's machine, resulting in code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The PDF is designed to exploit user trust and flawed warning dialog defaults to execute code, which is not a legitimate use of PDF scripting.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDFs may contain scripts for form validation or navigation, but should never download and execute remote code after user dialog interaction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise PDFs may use scripts for document automation, but never for remote code execution.
key_indicators: PDF triggers network request to download executable
Execution of payload after user accepts warning dialogs
Abuse of default dialog options to bypass user intent

attack_chain.action: User opens the malicious PDF in Foxit PDF Reader.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is presented with warning dialogs.

attack_chain.action: User clicks through two warning dialogs, both defaulting to the most harmful option.
PDF script downloads a payload from a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Payload is executed on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Remote payload is executed, potentially compromising the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: system compromise and possible further malware installation.

behavioral_signatures: PDF files that trigger network requests upon opening or after dialog interaction
Execution of downloaded payloads initiated by PDF scripts
Multiple warning dialogs with default options leading to code execution
file_indicators: PDFs with embedded JavaScript or launch actions
PDFs that reference external URLs for payload download
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests initiated by Foxit PDF Reader to unknown domains
Download of executable content following PDF file open event
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PDF files that contain embedded scripts or actions which initiate network connections or attempt to download executables. Alert on Foxit PDF Reader processes making outbound connections immediately after a PDF is opened, especially if followed by the creation or execution of new files. Analyze PDF structure for embedded JavaScript or launch actions referencing external resources.
